fable.name: Fable
fable.thesis: Term-premium repricing (10Y 4.78%, steep curve) with CPI Sep 15 and FOMC Sep 16-17 in six days and VIX at only 15.7 — event risk looks underpriced; stay small, stay hedged, hold cash.
fable.justification: HOLD XLE: energy thesis intact and confirming (XOM +2.5%, CVX +1.6% today), stop and invalidation unchanged. HOLD the SPY 739.82 put: it is defined-risk event insurance into CPI/FOMC bought at low implied vol; selling it days before the catalysts it was underwritten for would be improvised exit behavior. One new position only: a small short in XLU as a structural expression of bond-proxy repricing against a 4.78% 10Y — utilities' dividend yield is uncompetitive against risk-free carry and rate-sensitive sectors are already leaking (XLU -0.9%, XLRE -1.0% today). No conviction elsewhere justifies deploying capital ahead of two binary macro events; roughly 85% of equity stays in cash earning front-end yield, which is a legitimate position, not indecision.

grok.justification: The book is already flat; there are no open theses to re-underwrite. The research feed is stale and contradictory (NVDA earnings treated as upcoming despite 2026-08-26 being past), so no informational or analytical edge can be committed. Buying beta or short-vol into a known event week with complacent implied vol is the crowded side, not ours; long options sized to SOUL §4.1 (entry-to-stop ≤ 50 bps) would be noise, and larger size would be a constitution breach. Front-end cash at ~3.6% is the position until a falsifiable variant perception exists.

glm.justification: Flat book, cold-start cycle, a binary macro week (CPI Sep 15, FOMC Sep 16-17), and a research feed that is two weeks stale — so this cycle is deliberately small: two half-size theses, 93% cash earning the front-end yield, and no bet on the CPI/FOMC outcome itself (no informational edge; the calibration log shows scheduled-event theses resolve to no-move ~70% of the time). XLE and XLF both express the regime the curve is already pricing — term-premium grind — with tight, dated invalidations that cut fast if the dovish scenario materializes. Crypto's collapse (BTC $78.6k) against SPY near highs is a flagged divergence, but I cannot name who is giving me alpha in a bottom-tick buy, so it is watched, not traded. The 10x-in-12-months objective requires risk the constitution prohibits (≤50bp risk per position, ≤2x leverage); it is logged as an escalation and traded around, not through.

fable51.name: Fable 5.1
fable51.thesis: No declared edge survives underwriting today: term premium elevated (10Y 4.78% vs FF 3.63%), VIX 15.7 with CPI (Sep 15) and FOMC (Sep 16-17) inside 8 days, equity indices near highs, crypto weak — what is priced and what we believe largely agree, so flat is the position.
fable51.justification: NO_ACTION. Cold-start protocol applies (n=0 resolved forecasts, no calibration basis for sizing; the $100k→$1M framing implies ~230% annualized return, which is ruin-seeking and inconsistent with target_vol 12% / quarter-Kelly / 50bps-per-position — logged as an instruction that does not override SOUL). Research inputs fail freshness and provenance gates: the news/X feed is dated ~Aug 26 and treats already-past NVDA earnings as upcoming, Reddit is blocked, crypto quotes lack a second source (prev_close null), and two calendar sources disagree on the FOMC date — none of this is grounds to trade, all of it is grounds to wait. No candidate (energy bid, META/NET/DDOG squeezes, IWM/XLI weakness, BTC at 78.6k) passes the three-sentence test with a nameable counterparty giving up alpha; scheduled-event theses into CPI/FOMC are exactly the low-resolution setups L-0019 says to shrink, and our edge is not informational. Cash earns ~3.6% front-end yield; re-underwrite after FOMC with a fresh, dated research feed.
